15.notes: Hint 2 disposes of all three distractors in one sentence, so hint 3 is answerable without thinking. Hint 2 reads: 'The text does not blame tiredness or fear. Saul's men were an army hunting David, and they had no wish for David to kill Saul.' 'Does not blame tiredness or fear' rules out A and C, and 'had no wish for David to kill Saul' rules out B, leaving only D standing before hint 3 has done any work. A student who reads hint 2 already has the answer by elimination; hint 3's question about where the 'deep sleep' came from only confirms what hint 2 already gave away. The three-hint table is explicit that hint 2 must not 'state the answer, even indirectly.'
15.fix: Saul's men were an army hunting David; wanting David to kill Saul would not explain why every one of them was sound asleep. (Leave tiredness and fear unaddressed here so hint 3's question, 'did it come from their own bodies, or from somewhere else', still has two live possibilities to weigh against the Lord's doing.)

17.notes: Hint 2 disposes of all three distractors in one sentence, so hint 3 is answerable without thinking. Hint 2 reads: 'Solomon's reign was known for peace, not for leading Israel into battle. His building works and his choice of officials are not what the Bible says angered God.' This rules out A (battle), D (building works) and B (choice of officials, i.e. Jeroboam over labour) all at once, leaving only C standing before hint 3 has done any work. Hint 3 then asks 'of the options left, which one...' as if a genuine choice remained, but none does.
17.fix: Solomon's reign was known for peace, not for leading Israel into battle, so that option does not fit here. (Leave his building works and his choice of officials unaddressed so hint 3's question, about which decision broke a command God had given and led Solomon to worship other gods, still has real work to do.)

40.notes: The item contradicts itself about when the earthquake and the splitting of the rocks happened. Hint 2 says 'the earthquake and the splitting of the rocks come together,' and the Why-not-the-others line for D says the rocks split 'third, with the earthquake' (i.e. at the same moment as event two). But the How-to-tell list states them as two separate, sequential steps: 'Second: the earth shook.' and 'Third: the rocks were split.' A student who studies How-to-tell learns a strict four-stage sequence, then reads elsewhere in the same solution that stages two and three are actually one moment, which is a self-contradiction (check 11) and misstates the order of events as Matthew 27:51-52 actually reports them, in one clause together, not as separate stages (check 8). The exam tip repeats the same false sequencing by listing 'curtain, earthquake, rocks, tombs' as four discrete steps.
40.fix:
How to tell: follow Matthew's order.
First: the temple curtain was torn in two.
Then: the earth shook and the rocks were split together.
Last: the tombs were opened.

Why not the others:
A. earth shook: this happened together with the splitting of the rocks, straight after the curtain was torn.
C. tombs were opened: this came last of the four.
D. rocks split: this happened together with the earthquake, straight after the curtain was torn.

Exam tip: for 'which happened first' questions, learn the list in the Bible's own order, not by how dramatic each event seems. For Jesus' death in Matthew: the curtain was torn first, then the earth shook and the rocks split together, and the tombs opened last.

44.notes: The solution says: "Peter, who had denied Jesus out of fear a few weeks before, stood up and preached boldly." This timing is wrong. Peter's denial happened the night before the crucifixion, and Pentecost falls fifty days after that Passover (plus the few days to the resurrection), so the gap is roughly seven to eight weeks, not "a few weeks" (which reads as two to four).
44.fix: Peter, who had denied Jesus out of fear some seven weeks before, stood up and preached boldly.

45.notes: Hint 3 says: "The second purpose was about what Saul himself would go through for Jesus' name. Which option is about Saul's own experience rather than his work?" A student can answer this purely by scanning the wording of the four options, since only B ("show him how much he must suffer for Jesus") is phrased as something happening to Saul, while A, C and D are all phrased as things Saul does to or for others. No recall of Acts 9 is needed, so hint 3 lets the student answer without thinking, which the standard says makes it too strong.
45.fix: The Lord's words continue past 'to carry my name'. Recall what the rest of Acts 9:15-16 says would happen to Saul himself, and choose the option that matches it.

48.notes: Hint 3 says: "Peter says believers should grow up 'to' something by this milk. Which option names what a Christian grows into, rather than something the Lord does for them?" This can be solved from the wording of the options alone: B, C and D are all phrased as "the Lord will/can ... them", while A ("they will have salvation") is the only one phrased as a state the believer reaches. A student needs no knowledge of 1 Peter 2:2 to spot the odd one out this way, so hint 3 lets the student answer without thinking.
48.fix: Peter says believers should grow up 'to' something by this milk. Recall the last word of 1 Peter 2:2, and choose the option that names it.
